source_issues.detail: Intro attributes 6GB training to LoRA, while the table reserves it for QLoRA and gives fp16 LoRA ~18GB. Source 8B training sum 16GB+16GB+32GB=64GB even before activations, not 56GB. The 7B table uses a different model scale. Preserved, not silently corrected.

Exact target-module counts, benchmark scores, quality gaps and costs lack complete experiment/model/rank/hardware/sequence settings and traceable per-value citations. Values are faithfully preserved, not endorsed as measured results.

Theory uses column-vector BA with A:(r,d_in), B:(d_out,r); code uses transposed storage A:(d_in,r), B:(r,d_out) and x@A@B. Prose following code still says product BA, dimensionally incompatible with code variables in general. Retained.
Doc snippets mutate model.named_modules() traversal while iterating; code/lora.py uses list(model.named_modules()) snapshots. Doc snippets preserved unchanged.

quantize_to_nf4 is a uniform integer quantization simulation, not actual nonuniform NF4; it stores int8, not packed 4-bit. Doc reshape requires size divisible by 64, while code/lora.py pads. Actual model remains dequantized floating point in quantize_model. Source does call it a simulation; all code and wording retained.
Demo dimensions imply 14,336 adapter parameters and 399,370 base parameters, about 3.47% of total including adapters, not ~1%. Preserved.

Real-model Trainer snippet passes raw Alpaca rows without tokenization, labels or a collator. It is not a complete runnable SFT recipe. It also configures bfloat16 compute earlier while prose states fp16 adapters, and 6GB feasibility depends on unprovided setup. Not executed.

Costs, throughput, memory/quality percentages, recommended rank, exact NF4 quantile characterization, scaling-as-learning-rate language, merging guarantees and speed simplifications are broad or time-sensitive claims. No live verification under frozen-source scope; preserved.

For 7B weights, one 4-byte scale per 64 weights is 0.4375GB decimal; one byte per scale is 0.109375GB before secondary metadata. Source 0.4GB and 0.1GB are rounded. Correct block-of-64 relationship retained.
